rationale:
Issue #24 ("IdentifiedArray Equatable issues due to KeyPath") reports that two IdentifiedArrays holding identical elements compare unequal when their id key paths were formed in different contexts (generic `\.id` vs. an explicitly passed KeyPath), with a minimal reproducer in the issue body. The minimized production patch is exactly that defect's root cause: one hunk, one line, in IdentifiedArray+Equatable.swift changing `lhs.id == rhs.id && lhs.elementsEqual(rhs)` to `lhs.elementsEqual(rhs)`. No refactor, formatting, feature, docs, config, or test content is present in the minimized production patch (original_hunk_count=1, retained=1, removed=0, post_minimization_validation PASS). The trigger is the upstream test `testEquatable` added in the same commit; the curator reduction only rewrites `XCTAssertEqual(lhs, rhs)` as `XCTAssertTrue(lhs == rhs)` and `XCTAssertNotEqual(lhs, rhs)` as `XCTAssertTrue(lhs != rhs)` to avoid randomized type-context addresses in diagnostics. Those forms invoke the same `Equatable` conformance with the same expected relationships, and every construction, mutation, and iteration pair is preserved, so it is semantically equivalent. The test uses only initializers (`init()`, `init(uncheckedUniqueElements:id:)`, `init(uniqueElements:id:)`, and the Identifiable-constrained variants) that exist at the buggy revision; the fix introduces no new production API. Machine-generated strict evidence passes on both the original and post-minimization configurations: build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential PASS with reproduced selector `IdentifiedArrayTests.swift::testEquatable`, trigger.deterministic PASS (3 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions), trigger.fixed_clean PASS, full_suite.fixed_all_green PASS, and the buggy full suite fails only on the reproduced trigger. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and the proposed root_cause_id matches the single verified issue key in allowed_root_cause_ids (traceability.verified_fix_issue_numbers=[24], path fix_commit_to_issue via PR #25).

Issue #24 ('IdentifiedArray Equatable issues due to KeyPath') reports that two IdentifiedArrays holding identical elements compare unequal when their key paths were formed in different contexts (generic vs. concrete), with a minimal reproducer showing KeyPath equality failing. The minimized production patch is exactly that defect's root cause removal: one hunk, one line, in IdentifiedArray+Equatable.swift changing `lhs.id == rhs.id && lhs.elementsEqual(rhs)` to `lhs.elementsEqual(rhs)`. No formatting, refactor, doc, config, or test content is present in the minimized production patch (original_hunk_count=1, retained=1, removed=0, post_minimization_validation PASS). The trigger `IdentifiedArrayTests.testEquatable` is the upstream test from the same fix commit, only rewritten so `XCTAssertEqual(lhs, rhs)` becomes `XCTAssertTrue(lhs == rhs)` and `XCTAssertNotEqual(lhs, rhs)` becomes `XCTAssertTrue(lhs != rhs)`; for an Equatable type these assert the identical predicate via the same `==` witness, and the rewrite only avoids randomized type-context addresses in failure diagnostics. All arrays, initializers, mutations, and pairwise expectations are unchanged, and the test uses only initializers (`init()`, `init(uncheckedUniqueElements:id:)`, `init(uniqueElements:id:)`, and the Identifiable-constrained variants) that exist at the buggy revision 90628a5, so it depends on no API introduced by the fix. Strict machine evidence at both original and post-minimization stages passed every gate with no failed checks: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (1 unique selector), trigger.buggy_differential reproducing exactly testEquatable, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups), matrix.complete (32 runs, 3 repetitions), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and the proposed root cause equals the single allowed verified issue key, so it is not a duplicate.

risks: The dedicated issue_evidence field is null; the issue text relied on here comes from the embedded source_candidate.issue_check.linked_issues snapshot rather than an independent fetch.
KeyPath identity/uniquing is a compiler and runtime detail, so the differential may not reproduce on other Swift toolchain versions even though it is confirmed deterministic on the recorded matrix.

The final phase of the trigger asserts inequality between arrays with differing element values, which exercises general `==` behavior rather than the key path defect; a failure there would not be specific to this root cause.

The fix loosens equality by no longer comparing the id key path, so any downstream expectation of key-path-sensitive inequality changes behavior; the fixed full suite is green, but this is a semantic relaxation accepted upstream.
